reviews.comment: Lectures were the only bad part. Does proofs quietly without a mic, hard to follow without knowing concepts (Discrete, Notation, Symbols, Concepts). Explanations make it more confusing. Clear expectations and short homework&follows slides. Practice tests cover everything&Rvery similar. Tough lectures but well-planned. Only HW&Tests

MATH 304 at TAMU sucks in general, and Mandziuk only made it worse. Uninspired lecturing, and he never used the mic, so we could hardly hear him. Tough exams, and you never get them back to understand what you did wrong. Just horribly boring and hard to follow.

Not the best professor. I went to class sometimes but didn't really pay attention. mostly I studied through youtube. His canvas practice exams are super similar to actual exams which is great. Final exam was super hard (at least for me) but not cumulative tho it was the hardest unit imo. Self study and you will be fine!!

Professor Mandziuk often talked too quietly and was harder than other professors I have had in the past.  He uploads completed notes to Canvas, but his handwriting is also difficult to follow along with. It's not the worst in the world, and you'll be fine in his class as long as you show up to lectures, especially during line and surface integrals.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The way he writes, you'll confuse the letter "r" with "v" and "n," which really messes up your understanding at the beginning. He speaks so low and doesn't explain well, so going to class didn't help me most the time. He gives practice exams, but the actual exams are much much longer than them. I (and others) didn't fully finish even one exam.

I honestly stopped going to his class very early on. Talks very quietly and quickly which makes it hard to take notes, so I learned better on my own. In comparison to other sections, he tends to write harder/more questions on exams, and grades them pretty hard. Also not that helpful outside of class. You'll be okay but get someone else if you can.

Standard TAMU math class imo. Speaks fast and quiet with not the best handwriting in the world (Good luck telling an r from a n). Good balance of partial credit on exams but sometimes annoying with how many points are taken off for small issues. Final not technically cumulative. Homework on cengage and take home quiz on gradescope.

This prof talks very quiet and has little enthusiasm for the class. The lectures consist of him saying the letters/numbers as he does a problem and then moving on to the next. There was little time taken for the explanation of key topics. Time spent in class would be better spent reading the textbook or going to tutoring.

on average 2 homeworks per week on cengage and a quiz every week through gradescope, you have all day to do it and no time limit except due date. 4 tests, final not cumulative. He talks fast and has a bit of an accent but overall good professor.

I took Calculus 3 in high school and rarely attended lecture, but reviewed the provided notes before tests. Use online resources like OChem Tutor for clarification. Focus on understanding the intuition behind formulas, not just memorizing them. Grading is fair with lots of partial credit, so as long as you study, the tests are manageable.

He seems like a nice guy, but hes very quiet, his accent makes it hard to hear, his handwriting isn't great, and he moves through the notes extremely quick. His tests are pretty tough and sometimes too long for the time given. I do think he was somewhat fair with his grading. I think there are worse Calc III professors, but hes not the best.

He's a pretty chill guy. Exams were not terrible if you do the homework and pay attention, but he is very particular about details and will take points off. Quiet with an accent, but wasn't a problem for me. Tbh the only reason I got an A was bc I took multi in high school. He's super nice tho and helps as much as he can. Very cutie-patootie.

Great professor overall, with clear instruction throughout the semester. The class itself requires some effort. His final was hard which dropped my grade from an A to B.His accent is a little difficult to understand but I got used to it. This was his first semester at A&M so there is room for improvement.

He is a really good professor but hes not very begineer friendly. His lectures can be a bit fast paced and difficult to understand but if you focus and ask questions he will make sure you understand it. The homework isn't too bad and the quizzes are take home. Going to the Math Learning Center can be very helpful as well as the HOGU sessions.

Professor Mandziuk is a below average teacher with a hard to understand accent and extremely quiet voice that makes his lectures a challenge. His pacing of material is too quick in comparison to other professors and exams are lengthy for a 50 minute time period. Try to find another professor for Calculus III before registering for his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a pretty decent professor, if not a bit fast-paced. I personally didn't have a problem with his accent, but I can understand how others could. His quizzes are take home and his after hours were pretty helpful, especially before a test. Just make sure to do some practice work (and homework) before the exams and you'll be golden. Cutie-patootie.

His accent makes him difficult to understand, but otherwise he's fine. Helpful during office hours, responds fast to emails, and the weekly quizzes are take-home. I skipped almost all the lectures and got A's on the exams (but only because I did my hw + attended the HOGU sessions). ATTEND the HOGUs + do exam reviews, and you will be fine.
